newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan June index of leading indicators slides.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan June index of leading indicators slides.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecast peaks and troughs in the business cycle, fell slightly in June from May, a top economic planning agency said on Saturday.

The index edged down 0.2 of a percentage point to 103.2 in June on reduction in overall working hours in the manufacturing sector and customs revenues in June, the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said in a statement.
The index of coincident indicators, however, rose on increased production and cargo transportation, advancing 1.6 percent to 100 from a month earlier, the council said.
Overall the economy in June remained in a "green light" condition for the eighth straight month, indicating a gradual recovery and stable economic growth, the council said.

But the latest sample poll of manufacturing executives by the council showed that 17 percent predicted the economy would turn worse, up from May's 16. Nineteen percent thought it would improve, the same as the preceding month.
The rest said the economy would remain unchanged.
Analysts generally concur that Taiwan's economy is enjoying a modest recovery, spurred by improving export orders and healthy domestic consumption.

Economics minister Wang Chih-kang said on Tuesday the island would be untroubled reaching its target of 6.24 percent growth in gross domestic product in 1998 due to a steady rise in exports and investments.
